open.thesis: EUR rate path repriced dovish into the ECB while AUD carries the terms-of-trade tailwind from firm iron ore; the cross sits a full figure above where the 2yr spread says it belongs.

2s10s at +15bp after 18-month inversion. Buy 2Y (own cut optionality) vs short 10Y (short fiscal supply risk). June 5 payrolls at 89k + Fed pause re-prices front-end. ECB hiking cycle lifts global long rates. Steepener delivers whether Fed cuts or back-end sells off on supply. Late-cycle steepeners outperform after prolonged inversions.

Thursday's 25bp ECB hike is 99% priced — the rate-differential tailwind for EUR is in the price, and a hawkish US repricing widened the gap the other way. Classic buy-rumour-sell-fact setup into a fully-priced central bank. Pairs cleanly with long DAX: a weaker euro flatters the exporters.

closed.thesis: AVGO Q2 reports June 3. AI revenue guide 0.7B (+140% YoY) is the proof-of-concept for hyperscaler capex. Six consecutive AI revenue beats. Computex tailwind. Beat-and-raise moves stock 10-15%; in-line exits same day.

The Hormuz premium is Brent-specific — it prices the waterway, WTI prices Cushing. If the MoU frays, the Atlantic-basin grade reprices the de-mining risk and the spread widens; if it holds, physical caps the downside near current carry. A cleaner, lower-beta way to own the same re-escalation tail with defined spread risk.

The war premium has been removed from crude before the war risk has been removed from the Gulf. Tehran rejected the Friday MoU terms, US forces are staged to re-engage, and specs have cut net length from 191.9k to 178.8k — leaving squeeze fuel. Asymmetric: $7 of downside to the recent floor against $13 to a re-escalation reprice. This is the right-tail hedge on the book's barbell, not a directional call on peace.

closed.trade: Buy Brent $100/$115 call spread (own the Hormuz tail)
closed.thesis: The tail is firing: Israel struck western and central Iran Monday, US hit Iranian radar sites Friday, Iran fired missiles at Kuwait/Bahrain — and Brent gapped +3% to ~$96 with the MoU deadlocked on $24bn of frozen assets. A confirmed mine or tanker hit takes the Strait premium to $110+. Defined-risk momentum entry above spot; max loss the ~$3 premium if the Strait calms.

exit.reason: Peace deal deflated the Hormuz tail the call spread owned: with Brent ~$86 the $100 strike is $14 away and the catalyst is dead. Closed near the $1 discipline level to recover residual premium rather than ride a defined-risk position to zero.

closed.trade: Long DAX vs short Nasdaq Composite (ratio)
closed.thesis: Friday's selloff was a single-factor US event — AI concentration plus a hawkish payroll — and Europe decoupled outright (DAX +0.2% vs Nasdaq −4.2%). The ECB hikes Thursday into a financials-heavy index with no AI capex cycle to give back. Ratio entry 0.972 (DAX/Comp); the divergence has legs because it is structural, not sentiment.

VIX at 15.3 is cheap for 4 non-trivial events in 15 days: AVGO Jun 3, payrolls Jun 5, ECB Jun 11, FOMC Jun 16-17. 0.5% notional cost; 7x payoff if SPX draws down 6%. Insurance on a portfolio long AI equities.

exit.reason: BANKED into Jun-27 expiry. The FOMC-tail hedge did its job — peak ~$60 (+71%) as Warsh's hawkish dots dropped the S&P toward the strike and VIX re-rated to 18.4. With the Micron blowout ripping the tape back above the strike zone premarket (ES +0.78%) and one session to expiry, the residual is theta — harvested at ~$45 (+~29% from the ~$35 entry) rather than risk it bleeding to zero over the weekend. The replacement downside is the fresh Aug SPX put spread (MM-030).

closed.trade: Long gold into the June Fed window
closed.thesis: Pre-position into the 5 June payrolls / 16–17 June FOMC window. Gold has already decoupled from a 4.98% long bond, which means it is pricing both MoU tails at once. It wins if oil-disinflation forces a dovish Fed and real yields fall, AND it wins if the MoU fails and the geopolitical bid returns. It loses only on the narrow path of strong-growth + stable-oil + hawkish-Fed together. That is the asymmetry pre-positioning is built for; minimum 45-day hold, not an event-day scalp.
USDJPY at 159.37 with Finance Minister Katayama threatening intervention. BoJ September hike >50% priced vs Fed on hold. 3.63 pts downside to stop, 9.37 pts to target. Intervention is the backstop.

Brent −17% is a forward CPI cut the FedWatch distribution (67.8% no cuts in 2026) has not booked. Bonds already rallied 26bp off the 4.70% high; the disinflation impulse rolls headline lower into the autumn. Deliberately the opposite macro leg to the Brent longs — the book owns both sides of the MoU binary and gets paid on either resolution.

closed.trade: Short US 2Y yield (fade the hike, receive front-end)
closed.thesis: The market prices a ~70% hike by year-end on one 172k payroll with unemployment steady at 4.3%. The Fed does not hike into a labor market that is firm-but-not-overheating with a richly-valued equity tape just cracking. The 2-year at 4.16% — a 16-month high — has over-extrapolated a single number; the 17 June dot plot is the catalyst to reprice it. Pre-position, not an event scalp.

exit.reason: The trade's catalyst — a dovish 16-17 Jun FOMC repricing — resolved over two months ago with no exit taken. Today's data is the opposite regime: CME FedWatch prices 0% probability of a Sept cut and ~30% probability of a HIKE, and new Fed Chair Warsh goes into his first Jackson Hole keynote (Fri Aug 28) already signaling he is 'not constrained by market prices.' A short-front-end-yield trade built on rate-cut optionality has no business in the book heading into a hawkish setup. Closed near flat rather than let a stale thesis ride into an event that argues the other way.
